translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation of the future tense verb 'हँसोगे' (will laugh) and 'खोजेगी' (will seek) into the English present tense ('laugh', 'seeks') flattens the subtle shift from the present subjunctive/habitual framing of the first stanza to a more explicit future projection in the second stanza.

The Urdu-derived word 'नज़ाकत' (nazaakat), which carries deep aesthetic connotations of elegance, delicacy, and exquisite refinement in Hindustani poetic traditions, is translated as the more generic 'delicacy'.

annotation.theme: The subtle, sensory transformation of the world through the presence and actions of a beloved.

consistency_review_findings.issue: The stanza translation_quality is marked as 'partial' and the loss_note describes specific poetic and sensory losses, but the translation_loss array is empty. This is inconsistent; the described losses should be structured in the translation_loss array.

original_poem:
जब तुम्हारे हाथों की रेखाएँ  
खामोशी से कुछ कहने लगें,  
जब तुम्हारी आँखों में  
चाँदनी की खुशबू बसने लगे।  

जब तुम हँसोगे, और हवा  
तुम्हारे हँसने की आवाज़ में  
लय खोजेगी,  
जब हर पल की नज़ाकत  
तुमसे जुड़ने लगे।
translated_poem:
When the lines of your hands  
Begin to speak silently,  
When the fragrance of moonlight  
Resides in your eyes.  

When you laugh, and the breeze  
Seeks a rhythm in your laughter,  
When the delicacy of every moment  
Starts to connect with you.
